headline: Sunday answered Saturday with escalation: Riyadh struck twice in 24 hours, the Houthis formally claimed it and named Aramco as a target, and the Mecca pact started deploying — the 5pm CT reopen reprices a widening war, one hour after this edition.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: Sunday stacked the war ledger again — a second strike on Riyadh, a formal Houthi claim naming Aramco, Trump's 'you're gonna find out' on joining the Saudi campaign. The hawkish hold rides into CPI week untouched; the reopen is a war repricing, not a Fed repricing.
chapters.meaning: What changed: Sunday answered Saturday with escalation, not diplomacy. A second projectile struck Riyadh's King Khalid airport — fire in Terminal 4, an unspecified number injured (GACA), a cruise missile intercepted nearby. The Houthi military formally claimed Saturday's strike for the first time (13 killed, 300+ wounded — an Indian national died Sunday, raising the toll) and named new targets: Dammam airport, which GACA confirmed was attacked Sunday, plus two Aramco facilities — the Shedgum gas station and the Tanajib refinery — which are claimed, not confirmed by Saudi/Aramco. Sanaa's airport was hit too, so airports on both sides of the war are now targets. The war internationalized: Turkey and Pakistan are deploying to Saudi Arabia under the Mecca pact (defensive and technical roles — equipment, intel sharing, air defence), Syria sent drone operators to Aden, US military and intelligence operatives are already in the kingdom assisting with targeting, Britain is refuelling Saudi jets, and France has troops and radar there. Trump, back at Joint Base Andrews: 'we have communication with the Houthis,' he'll speak to MBS, and on joining the Saudi campaign — 'you're gonna find out.' Thread: the hawkish hold is in week four — Dec ~80% priced, Oct ~18% (CME FedWatch); claims held 197k for a fourth straight week; Saturday's maritime escalation (IRGC mine claim, tanker #18, the Ocean Molica disabled) still stands. What it means: confirms. Sunday added zero Fed-relevant data — the dollar's path into CPI week is unchanged — but the haven ledger into the reopen is now heavier on the escalation side than at 2am, with the diplomacy side (Putin's broker channel, Trump's no-strike-before-midterms pledge) still the only counterweight. Note the split in Washington: Rubio condemned the strike that killed an American — 'They must stop now' — while the US Mission issued a security alert steering Americans clear of Saudi airports.
chapters.fx: What to watch: the Sunday 5pm CT reopen — the first price test of Sunday's airport campaign; watch USD/JPY and USD/CHF for haven gaps. Monday is Columbus Day: US bond markets are closed, Japan and Canada shut — thin liquidity amplifies moves while FX spot trades normally. Then the real week: US CPI Wednesday 7:30am CT (consensus 3.6% y/y, core 2.5% — the key number is core m/m at 0.2%), Fed Chair Warsh speaks Thursday 10:30pm CT — his read on the prints decides whether the hawkish hold becomes a hike. Diplomacy side: the MBS call outcome and whether Trump picks up Putin's broker channel. Friday's Truth Social post (productive Iran talks, no Iran strike before the midterms) still stands as the ceiling on the US–Iran track.
numbers: US CPI Wed 7:30am CT (3.6% y/y fcst); Warsh Thu 10:30pm CT

scenarios.base: Hawkish hold rides through CPI week; havens gap on the open, then the market waits for Wednesday's prints.
scenarios.bull: Hot CPI (core 0.3%+) takes October back off the table — the dollar extends.
scenarios.bear: Diplomacy breakthrough on the MBS call or a soft CPI — the haven bid unwinds and DXY gives back.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: Sunday's Ukraine energy-ceasefire theater collapsed within hours — Zelensky called it 'news for me,' Russia struck Zaporizhzhia anyway. The euro goes into Monday at ~1.12 with nothing clearing Europe's energy risk premium.
chapters.meaning: What changed: Trump announced an 'ENERGY CEASEFIRE ... Effective immediately' between Russia and Ukraine on Sunday morning — but the WSJ notes it's the same deal he announced Sept. 14, and both sides kept striking then too. Sunday's version died faster: Zelensky told ABC's This Week the announcement was 'news for me' (open to it if reciprocal, with elections for a 60-day truce); hours later Russian airstrikes killed at least 23 people in Zaporizhzhia, and Russia kept bombing Kyiv's energy grid all day; the Kremlin never confirmed. A parallel lever surfaced: the FT, via Reuters, reports the US is threatening to shut the PURL arms-procurement pipeline to Ukraine and cut intelligence sharing to force Kyiv to halt deep strikes on Russian refineries — Reuters could not independently confirm it and the White House didn't respond, so it stays a report, not a fact. The revolt against the diesel deal went bipartisan at home Sunday: seven senators (4 GOP, 3 Dem) demanded the administration 'immediately reverse course,' arguing it violates Congress's 2022 Russian energy-import ban — Sen. Tillis: a 'legitimate case' the president is 'not following the law'; Bessent dug in on Fox News Sunday. And the transatlantic split is showing: UK PM Burnham told Zelensky the UK keeps its 'toughest sanctions regime ever' and will not follow the US in buying Russian diesel. Thread: EUR/USD ~1.12, the 17-month low at 1.1161 held, the French fiscal dossier quiet until Tuesday's budget plenary. What it means: confirms the morning's quiet read — Europe's energy risk premium clears on verifiable deals, not social-media posts. The refinery-and-diesel pressure on European energy stays live, and the US pressure campaign on Kyiv is now about squeezing the weapons flow, not just words.
chapters.fx: What to watch: any Kremlin confirmation of the ceasefire (don't hold your breath); whether Moscow's grid bombing pauses; the Sunday 5pm CT oil and diesel open as the market's vote on the theater; French budget plenary Tuesday (OAT–Bund ~140–146bp is the fuse); OPEC+ Nov 1.

scenarios.bull: A verified energy de-escalation or a calm French budget vote — 1.12 breaks higher.
scenarios.bear: Grid strikes continue and French fiscal stress flares — 1.1161 gives way.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: Sterling spent the weekend doing nothing — $1.324, the floor at 1.3180 still holding. Bailey speaks twice this week; that's the chapter.
chapters.meaning: What changed: nothing for sterling — the weekend's action was all Gulf. Thread: GBP/USD ~1.324, flat Friday; EUR/GBP at 84.74p is a 16-month sterling high; the November 5 BoE hike is ~85% priced with the 30Y gilt above 6%. What it means: the hawkish-BoE floor thesis stands unchallenged — the only thing leaning on sterling into Monday is its risk-proxy side, with the war ledger heavier than at 2am.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Bailey's two speeches this week; UK GDP Thursday (fcst −0.1% m/m) — a negative print tests the hiking story; haven gaps on the Sunday open.

scenarios.bull: Hot UK CPI cements the November hike — GBP/USD pushes toward 1.34.
scenarios.bear: A Budget that spooks gilts — GBP gives back the euro-driven gains fast.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: Sunday handed the yen a second serving — Riyadh struck again, a formal Houthi claim naming Aramco, Mecca-pact deployments. USD/JPY 158.26 goes into the reopen with fear stacking against the rate gap.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the haven ledger thickened — a second Riyadh strike in 24 hours, the formal Houthi claim with oil-infrastructure targets named, Dammam confirmed, Mecca-pact troops moving, Trump's 'you're gonna find out.' Thread: USD/JPY 158.26 (+0.3% Fri); CFTC yen net longs rebuilt to 62,325 (week to Oct 6, up from 55,440); BoJ December hike >80% priced (OIS) against the US 10Y at 5.24–5.26% — the rate gap pulls toward 159–160 while fear pulls toward 155. What it means: confirms the morning's two-way tug — Sunday just put more weight on the fear side of the scale.
chapters.fx: What to watch: the Sunday open's gap in USD/JPY — a risk-off gap lower is the fear read; Monday's thin liquidity (Japan shut for Sports Day) amplifies; BoJ December pricing holds above 80% unless CPI week reprices the Fed.
numbers: CFTC JPY net longs 62,325 (wk to Oct 6; up from 55,440)

scenarios.base: Rate gap dominates; USD/JPY consolidates below 159–160 while intervention talk caps the top.
scenarios.bull: Sunday's escalation gaps at the reopen — the yen rallies and USD/JPY breaks lower through 158.
scenarios.bear: The reopen shrugs at the weekend news; the yield gap reasserts and 159–160 comes back into play.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The franc's job got even simpler — a pure fear barometer, and Sunday stacked the fear: two Riyadh strikes in 24 hours and a formal claim naming Aramco.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the fear stacked up twice over — a second Riyadh strike Sunday (Terminal 4 fire, cruise missile intercepted) plus the formal Houthi claim naming oil infrastructure as a target. Thread: USD/CHF 0.8302 (−0.17% Fri); SNB pinned at 0.00% with no domestic rate story. What it means: the franc's read is one-dimensional right now — it firms into the reopen on Sunday's escalation, and that's the whole chapter.
chapters.fx: What to watch: the Sunday open's USD/CHF gap — that's the pure fear gauge; Schlegel speaks Thursday.

scenarios.base: CHF firms into the reopen on Sunday's escalation; USD/CHF drifts lower.
scenarios.bull: Fresh escalation — CHF extends as the fear trade.
scenarios.bear: The reopen shrugs — the haven bid leaks out again.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The cleanest risk proxy goes into Sunday's open with the escalation ledger stacked against it — and the RBI's dollar window adds an Asia-FX wrinkle for Monday.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the risk mood darkened — two Riyadh strikes, the Houthi claim naming Aramco, Mecca-pact deployments. Thread: AUD/USD ~0.6986 (−0.11% Fri, the weakest G8 name late Friday); RBA on hold at 4.60% after the Sep 29 hike, minutes out Monday 7:30pm CT; the rupee near record lows (~96.7) with the RBI's dollar window for oil companies opening Monday; China: Hang Seng +1.5% Friday, yuan ~6.694. What it means: the cleanest risk proxy carries Sunday's escalation into the open with nothing domestic to offset it — the minutes Monday night are the first real domestic input.
chapters.fx: What to watch: the Sunday open's gap — escalation means a softer open; RBA minutes Monday 7:30pm CT (any hawkish lean from the Sep 29 hike); the rupee and RBI window Monday; Australia jobs later in the week.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: Sunday thickened Brent's floor again — but the 161bp rate gap still owns the loonie at 18-month lows going into the open.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the war premium's floor got thicker — two Riyadh strikes in 24 hours, the formal Houthi claim naming Aramco infrastructure, Mecca-pact deployments; Brent goes into the 5pm CT open at $104.72 with gap risk toward $106–108. Thread: USD/CAD 1.4257, 18-month CAD lows held; Oct 28 BoC hike odds ~25% (from 40% pre-jobs); the US–Canada 2Y gap at ~161bp, widest since February 2025; and the number that actually moves Canada's terms of trade is WTI (~$91.8) — with the Brent–WTI spread near $13, the WTI leg of the war premium stays muted. What it means: the tug-of-war continues — war premium for the loonie against the rate gap owning it. Sunday strengthened the first hand, not the second.
chapters.fx: What to watch: the 5pm CT open's Brent gap — that IS the CAD read overnight; Macklem speaks twice this week; Canada CPI Oct 21; BoC Oct 28.

scenarios.base: Tug-of-war holds; USD/CAD consolidates near 1.42–1.43 into the BoC.
scenarios.bull: Brent gaps toward $108 and holds — the oil offset finally bites and the loonie firms.
scenarios.bear: The reopen shrugs the weekend news; the 161bp gap reasserts and 18-month lows break.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Sunday moved the war off the shipping lanes and onto infrastructure — Riyadh struck again, Dammam confirmed, Aramco named as a target — and the war went international. The ~$13 Brent–WTI spread goes into the 5pm CT open with fresh reason to stay wide.
chapters.meaning: What changed: Sunday escalated the airport campaign. A second projectile struck Riyadh's King Khalid airport (Terminal 4 fire; a cruise missile intercepted nearby; unspecified injuries, per GACA). GACA confirmed King Fahd airport in Dammam was attacked Sunday. The Houthi military formally claimed Saturday's strike (13 killed) and named oil infrastructure — the Aramco Shedgum gas station and the Tanajib refinery — as targets; the Aramco claims are not confirmed by Saudi or Aramco, treat them as claims. Meanwhile the war's footprint widened: Turkey and Pakistan deploying to Saudi Arabia under the Mecca pact (defensive/technical — equipment, intel sharing, air defence), Syria's drone operators in Aden, US military-intel operatives already assisting Saudi targeting, Britain refuelling Saudi jets, France with troops and radar in the kingdom. Airlines are pulling out, not delaying: Air France suspended Riyadh through Oct 24, Air India through Oct 15, 600+ flights canceled, Riyadh schools remote through Thursday. The parallel Ukraine track went theatrical: Trump's Sunday-morning 'energy ceasefire' was contradicted by Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia within hours and all-day bombing of Kyiv's grid, and the FT reports the US threatening to cut Ukraine's arms pipeline to stop refinery strikes (unconfirmed). Thread: Brent settled Friday at $104.72 (+$0.44, +2.42% on the week — verified against Investing.com historical data); the ~$13 gap to WTI (~$91.8) is the geopolitical and shipping premium living in Brent while landlocked WTI barely feels it; Hormuz transits sit at two-month lows; the Gulf of Mexico storm still has 511k b/d shut in (a WTI-side supply factor). What it means: confirms the morning's wide-spread thesis — Sunday's escalation is all Brent-side premium; WTI is the demand and storm-restart number.
chapters.fx: What to watch: the 5pm CT open is the price test — watch whether crude gaps toward $106–108; the MBS call and Trump's decision on joining the Saudi campaign; Gulf of Mexico restart figures through the week; the EIA weekly (the first to capture storm shut-ins in full); OPEC+ Nov 1. The spread itself is the gauge: past $15 means Hormuz risk is back in force; toward $5 means the premium is truly unwinding. On the diesel front: the Senate revolt and Bessent's legal fight decide whether the Russian diesel flow survives — that flow is the bear case for refined-product tightness.

scenarios.bear: The MBS call yields diplomacy, flows hold, GoM restarts fast — Brent under $100, spread collapses toward $5.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold goes into Sunday's open with both legs loaded — the anti-dollar and the war hedge — and Sunday re-armed the second one twice over.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the war-hedge leg got two servings — a second Riyadh strike in 24 hours and the formal Houthi claim naming Aramco as a target. Thread: spot ~$4,195 Friday, ~22% below the January $5,318 all-time high; the anti-dollar leg waits on Wednesday's CPI (consensus 3.6% y/y; a soft core m/m at 0.2% or below weakens the dollar leg and re-arms gold). What it means: confirms — gold is the one chapter where both engines are pointed the same way into the reopen.
chapters.fx: What to watch: the Sunday open's haven gap; Wednesday's CPI — the dollar leg decides; hot CPI (core 0.3%+) revives October-hike talk, real yields jump, and gold slides back toward $4,000.
